correct_completion: she submitted it to the committee before the deadline.
full_sentence: Having finished the report, she submitted it to the committee before the deadline.
acceptable_variants: she sent it to the committee before the deadline.
she handed it in to the committee ahead of schedule.

options.text: the committee has submitted it before the deadline.
options.why_wrong: The participle clause implies that the subject finished the report, but the committee did not finish it, so the subjects do not match.

options.text: she submitted it to the committee before the deadline.
the report was finally submitted to the committee.
options.why_wrong: The main clause makes the report the subject, while the participle clause implies a person finished it, so the two clauses do not share a subject.

options.text: while the committee was waiting for it.
options.why_wrong: This adds a background detail, but the main clause must be a complete action performed by the same subject as the participle clause.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a shared subject
explanation: A participle clause at the start of a sentence must refer to the same subject as the main clause. Learners often transfer gerund or infinitive-style constructions directly from their first language, but in English the subject of the participle clause must be the person who performs the main action.
translation: Tendo terminado o relatório, ela o enviou à comissão antes do prazo.
